findings.summary: update_email writes to the database but never invalidates the read-through cache, so get_user keeps returning stale data.
findings.failure_scenario: Call get_user(1) (caches the user record with old email), then update_email(1, "new@example.com") which updates only the DB. A subsequent get_user(1) finds user_id still in self._cache and returns the stale cached record with the old email instead of "new@example.com". The cache entry must be popped/updated in update_email.

findings.summary: update_email writes to the database but never invalidates or updates the in-memory read-through cache, so get_user returns stale data.
findings.failure_scenario: Call get_user(1), which populates self._cache[1] with the user record (email "old@x.com"). Then call update_email(1, "new@x.com"), which updates the DB but leaves self._cache[1] unchanged. A subsequent get_user(1) finds user_id in self._cache and returns the stale record with "old@x.com" instead of the updated "new@x.com". Fix: after db.update_user, invalidate (e.g., self._cache.pop(user_id, None)) or update the cached entry.

findings.summary: compute_discount ignores each line item's 'type', so non-discountable items (e.g. gift cards) are wrongly included in the discount base.
findings.failure_scenario: Given line_items=[{"price": 5000, "type": "gift_card"}], if gift cards are not eligible for a coupon, the function still returns min(5000*1000//10000, 2000)=500 cents of discount instead of 0. The docstring highlights 'type' but the code never filters on it.

findings.summary: compute_discount ignores each item's 'type', so it applies the coupon discount to non-discountable items (e.g. gift cards) instead of excluding them from the discount base.
findings.failure_scenario: Given line_items=[{"price": 5000, "type": "gift_card"}], compute_discount returns min(5000*1000//10000, 2000)=500, applying a $5.00 discount to a gift card. The docstrings pointedly note every item has a 'type', implying certain types must be excluded from the discountable base, but 'type' is never read, so ineligible items are discounted.
